clue.text: Tear off to be entertained by thin relation

indicators.note: something entertained by a host is taken in, so these letters sit inside the other word

parts.note: gaunt means thin and haggard

indicators.note: off here means out of order or wrong, so the letters of the word tear are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone storms off to be hosted by a skinny family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' looks like a verb of rushing away, but its letters are the fodder, rearranged by 'off' into REAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's aunt is a family member, so she is a relation.

clue.text: Allocates new chairs to each in the course of breaks

indicators.note: something occurring in the course of a span lies within it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: rests are breaks or pauses

explanation.surface: Someone shuffles the seating plan for everyone during intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a different seat is to put them in a new place to sit, i.e. new chairs.

clue.text: Claim of abbot's number two based on logic

indicators.note: of here frames the claim around the speaker's title, so the title sits inside the claim's words

parts.note: the claim is the deputy saying 'a ... I', i.e. 'I am a prior', giving the words A and I around the title
in a monastery the prior ranks just below the abbot

explanation.surface: A monk's deputy asserts something, apparently on rational grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The deputy's claim reads 'A PRIOR, I' — he declares himself a prior. The Latin phrase means reasoning from first principles rather than experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'from what comes before': knowledge reached by deduction rather than observation.

clue.text: A right uninteresting person leading volunteers in the woods

indicators.note: the first pieces lead, coming before the volunteers' letters

parts.note: a bore is a tedious person
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A dull man heads a team of volunteers out among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboreta are tree collections planted for study, so they are a kind of woods.

clue.text: Food should be put under grill? Not egg

indicators.note: not signals that the following item is left out of the word

parts.note: bread put under a grill is toasted
O looks like an egg, a crossword convention for the letter

explanation.surface: Advice for the kitchen: grill your food, but leave out the egg.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'Food should be [tasted]': a cook samples food before serving. TOASTED loses its O.
explanation.definitionFit: Food is sampled to check its flavour, which is what a cook means by having it checked in the mouth.

clue.text: Message to encourage escape of Charlie's bonny vessel

definitions.text: Message to encourage escape of Charlie's bonny vessel

parts.words: Message to encourage escape of Charlie's bonny vessel
parts.note: the Skye Boat Song, about Bonnie Prince Charlie fleeing, begins 'Speed, bonnie boat': speed urges flight, and the boat is the vessel

explanation.surface: A rallying cry for a royal fugitive's handsome boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Skye Boat Song, a Scottish song about Bonnie Prince Charlie's 1746 flight to Skye, opens 'Speed, bonnie boat'. The answer is also a fast motor launch.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast motorised launch is a vessel, and the song's opening words urge the boat to go quickly.

clue.text: What could make lass cry in a silly manner?

indicators.note: asks what the letters could be made into, so the words lass and cry are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks what tactless act would bring a girl to tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass means grossly stupid or insensitive, so the adverb means foolishly.

clue.text: Area misunderstood puts learner in annoying situation, awkward position

indicators.note: the learner is put in, inside the word for the annoying situation

parts.note: a bind is a nuisance or tight spot
L is for learner, as on British L-plates
to be in a spot is to be in difficulty

explanation.surface: A trainee gets into a tight corner and an uncomfortable fix.
explanation.walkthrough: L, from British learner-driver plates, goes inside BIND.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic someone consistently fails to grasp is a gap in their understanding, an area they cannot see.

clue.text: Clothes are left, found behind a piano more than once

indicators.note: the remaining letters come behind, after the opening ones
the piano letter appears twice here, so it is repeated

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Garments abandoned behind a piano, several times over.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for clothing or garments.

clue.text: Attribute of a writer

parts.note: a scribe is a copyist or writer

explanation.surface: A quality belonging to an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attribute' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit something to a source is to attribute it, the verb sense.

clue.text: Time to argue for disloyalty

parts.note: to reason is to argue logically

explanation.surface: It is time to make the case for betrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country or sovereign is the gravest form of disloyalty.

clue.text: Virtue of a disciplined pet

indicators.note: disciplined letters are knocked into a new order, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The good qualities of a well-trained animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher's pet is the preferred one, so pet is a synonym for the most-liked person.

clue.text: Rose and Dorothy after upset were kept inside

indicators.note: the word were is held within the other piece
in a down clue upset turns the word over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Dot is a short form of the name Dorothy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two women, Rose and Dorothy, were detained after an upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the short name round to TOD. 'Rose' is not a woman but the past tense of rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose is the past tense of rise, and towered is the past tense of soaring high above.

clue.text: Strange folk dances led by old theologian

indicators.note: the dances come after, led by the earlier pieces

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree
balls are formal dances

explanation.surface: Peculiar people at dances headed by an elderly religious scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentric people are odd ones out, unconventional characters.

clue.text: Fool is last to accept help

parts.note: an ass is a fool
taken as written

indicators.note: the last letter of accept is the one taken

explanation.surface: An idiot is the final person to take any aid.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid someone is to give them assistance, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Designer of the thing seen in cunning form of therapy

indicators.note: something seen in another is contained within it

parts.note: arch means sly or knowing
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy
it is the pronoun for the thing

explanation.surface: Whoever created that device spotted in a crafty treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: One who draws up plans for buildings is their designer.

clue.text: Support for injury having got hit in fighting?

indicators.note: the blow is placed in, within the word for the support

parts.note: a sling supports an injured arm
to cuff is to strike with an open hand

explanation.surface: Someone wears an arm brace after being struck in a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A scuffle is a short confused fight, so the gerund means brawling.

clue.text: A President in small room is joined by a star

indicators.note: the final piece is attached after the rest
the first pieces go in, inside the small room

parts.note: a cell is a small room

explanation.surface: A head of state in a tiny room is joined by a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: AP goes inside CELL, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Capella is the brightest star in the constellation Auriga.

clue.text: Lady Fortune, for Spooner, one no longer effective

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first consonants are exchanged

parts.note: a dame is a titled lady
Lady Luck personifies fortune

explanation.surface: Lady Luck, as the muddled Reverend would say, describes a has-been.
explanation.walkthrough: DAME LUCK swaps its initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An official serving out a term after a successor is chosen has lost power: a powerless figure.

clue.text: Islands in grip of evil Italian breaking the law

parts.note: ill can mean evil, as in ill will

indicators.note: held in the grip of means enclosed, so the islands go inside

parts.note: CI stands for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Islanders held by a wicked Italian who flouts the law.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands lie off Normandy and belong to the British Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlawful is forbidden by law, so it breaks the law.

clue.text: One shouldering heavy burden — tons at the end

parts.note: the Titan Atlas carried the heavens on his shoulders

explanation.surface: A weightlifter finally hoists tonnes of load.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means finally, after a long wait, which is when the end comes.

clue.text: European valiant in battle

indicators.note: letters in battle are thrown into disorder, so valiant is rearranged

explanation.surface: A brave Continental soldier in combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from a Baltic state is a native of Europe.

clue.text: Do better than basic success in exam after teacher is listened to

indicators.note: the exam success comes after the teacher's piece
listening points to how the word for teacher is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: sir is how pupils address a male teacher
a pass is the minimum success in an exam

explanation.surface: A pupil scrapes through an exam after paying attention to the teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: SIR, the British schoolchild's address for a male teacher, gives SUR by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed or outdo someone is to perform better than them.

clue.text: Don't yet try to kill the fellow hugging ancient tree!

indicators.note: a piece that hugs another wraps around it

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
old means ancient
a fir is a conifer

explanation.surface: A man embraces an old tree, and someone shouts at the hunter to wait.
explanation.definitionFit: The order to refrain from shooting means delaying any attempt to shoot.

clue.text: Sailor chattering, not quiet at first

indicators.note: not signals removing the quiet letter
the removal happens at the front of the word

parts.note: prating means talking foolishly at length
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: A talkative seaman who was silent at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating is a naval seaman without officer's rank.

clue.text: Coming to northern river for exciting experience

parts.note: advent means an arrival or coming
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Arriving at a river up north for a thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure flows through North Yorkshire in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrilling or daring undertaking is an exciting experience.

clue.text: One of three kids scattering litter round front of park

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the next piece
scattering spreads the letters of litter about into a new order
the front of park is its first letter

explanation.surface: Children dropping rubbish all around the park entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattering' rearranges LITTER into TRILET, which goes round P.
explanation.definitionFit: Three children born at one birth are each one of a set of three.

clue.text: Greek character thus joins leader of Gang Show

indicators.note: the gang leader joins on after the other pieces

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
sic is Latin for thus
Al Capone was the notorious gang leader

explanation.surface: A Greek actor joins the lead of a Gang Show, a Scouting revue.
explanation.walkthrough: AL is Al Capone, the gangster. The Gang Show is a British Scout variety revue.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage production with songs and dance is a type of show.

clue.text: Hair that could be inch long with initial cut

indicators.note: says what the letters could become, so they are rearranged
the first letter of long is removed

explanation.surface: A hairstyle that might be an inch in length, its tip trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: LONG loses its L, and INCH plus ONG are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A coil of tresses worn at the nape of the neck is a hairstyle, so the definition is hair.

clue.text: Quality of ungainly person offering weak signs taken amiss

indicators.note: amiss means wrongly, so the letters are taken in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A clumsy person shows feeble signs that are misunderstood.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkwardness and clumsiness is the trait of someone gangly or ungainly.
